title: Composition isomorphisms of derived direct images (conjugates of those of inverse images)
statement:
Let $u:Y\to X$ and $v:Z\to Y$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with the derived direct images $Ru_*,Rv_*,R(u\circ v)_*,R(\mathrm{id}_X)_*$ on the bounded below derived categories of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the adjunctions $w^{-1}\dashv Rw_*$ with unit $\eta^D_w$ and counit $\varepsilon^D_w$ [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction] (for $w=u$, $v$, $u\circ v$ and $\mathrm{id}_X$), and the composition and identity isomorphisms $c^D_{u,v}:v^{-1}u^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(u\circ v)^{-1}$, $e^D_X:\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ of the derived inverse images [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition]. Let $v^{-1}u^{-1}\dashv Ru_*Rv_*$ be the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] of $u^{-1}\dashv Ru_*$ and $v^{-1}\dashv Rv_*$ (unit $Ru_*\eta^D_vu^{-1}\circ\eta^D_u$, counit $\varepsilon^D_v\circ v^{-1}\varepsilon^D_uRv_*$), and $\mathrm{id}\dashv\mathrm{id}$ the identity adjunction on $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. The *composition isomorphism of derived direct images*
$$
 d^D_{u,v}:R(u\circ v)_*\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Ru_*\circ Rv_*
$$
is the conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] of $c^D_{u,v}:v^{-1}u^{-1}\to(u\circ v)^{-1}$ with respect to $L_1=(u\circ v)^{-1}\dashv R_1=R(u\circ v)_*$ and $L_2=v^{-1}u^{-1}\dashv R_2=Ru_*Rv_*$; and the *identity isomorphism* $d^D_X:R(\mathrm{id}_X)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ is the conjugate of $(e^D_X)^{-1}:\mathrm{id}\to\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}$ with respect to $L_1=\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}\dashv R_1=R(\mathrm{id}_X)_*$ and $L_2=\mathrm{id}\dashv R_2=\mathrm{id}$ (equivalently, the inverse of the conjugate $\mathrm{id}\to R(\mathrm{id}_X)_*$ of $e^D_X$). Both are isomorphisms because $c^D_{u,v}$ and $(e^D_X)^{-1}$ are: conjugation sends isomorphisms to isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Explicitly, $d^D_{u,v,K}$ is the composite $R(uv)_*K\xrightarrow{\eta}Ru_*Rv_*v^{-1}u^{-1}R(uv)_*K\xrightarrow{Ru_*Rv_*c^D_{u,v}}Ru_*Rv_*(uv)^{-1}R(uv)_*K\xrightarrow{Ru_*Rv_*\varepsilon^D_{uv,K}}Ru_*Rv_*K$, $\eta$ the unit of the composite adjunction, and $d^D_{X,K}$ is the composite $R(\mathrm{id}_X)_*K\xrightarrow{(e^D_{X})^{-1}}\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}R(\mathrm{id}_X)_*K\xrightarrow{\varepsilon^D_{\mathrm{id}_X,K}}K$.

split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks 0D6E (sites-cohomology.tex line 4011: Rg_*Rf_* is adjoint to Lf^*Lg^* = L(gf)^*, hence equal to R(gf)_* by uniqueness of adjoints). Notions: the derived adjunctions (prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction), c^D and e^D (lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition), the conjugate (def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate, Mathlib leaf; it also carries the only claim inside, that the conjugate of an isomorphism is an isomorphism, by conjugateIsoEquiv), and the composite and identity adjunctions, which no node named: new Mathlib leaf def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction (Adjunction.comp, Stacks 0DV0; Adjunction.id). Corrected the identity clause: conjugation reverses direction (conjugateEquiv : (L2 -> L1) ≃ (R1 -> R2)), so the conjugate of e^D_X : id_X^{-1} -> id is a map id -> R(id_X)_*, not R(id_X)_* -> id; d^D_X is now the conjugate of (e^D_X)^{-1}, with its explicit formula. The composition clause had the right direction. The definition claims neither the agreement of d^D with the identification R(uv)_*K = (uv)_*I = u_*v_*I on a K-injective I nor associativity/unitality of d^D, and its one user (lem-weil-pbc-exchange-identity-pasting) uses neither, so no statement node was created for them. Mathlib re-searched three ways: no composition isomorphism of derived functors or derived pushforwards in Mathlib.
